rooms.16200: A large log cabin squats on a bare shoulder of hillside, its walls grey with weather and its shutters nailed fast. A narrow path winds east into the mist toward the high mountain path. The grass here grows in pale, wrong tufts, and no bird sings anywhere. A heavy door in the cabin wall stands a little ajar to the south, and the roofline leans like a thing that is listening.
rooms.16202: A narrow front hall of dark pine boards, hung with coat pegs that hold only shadows. The floor is polished so smooth that the lamplight slides along it like oil. A door north opens back onto the hillside, a door east leads to a living room, and another west into a library, while the hall itself goes on south. The beams overhead sit a hand's breadth too low at one end and too high at the other.
rooms.16203: A broad living room with a cold hearth of fieldstone and chairs drawn up around it as though for a gathering that never came. The chairs have too many legs for their size, or too few, and your eye will not settle on which. A threadbare rug lies under dust as thick as felt. The only way out is the door back west into the hall.
rooms.16205: The hall bends here into its lower reach, where the floorboards run crosswise to the ones behind you and the lamps burn a dull orange. Doors stand east and west, one to a bedroom and one to a kitchen, and a third door south gives onto a room that glitters. The front of the hall lies north. The wallpaper repeats a pattern of tiny closed eyes, and the quiet in this place seems to lean toward you.
rooms.16206: A bedroom with a tall bed hung in rotting curtains, its coverlet pulled smooth as if no one had ever slept in it. The wardrobe stands against the wall at a tilt that should send it crashing down, yet it does not. A candle stub has melted into the sill in a long pale tongue, and the window shows only a flat grey that is not sky. The door west is the only way back to the hall.
rooms.16207: Mirrors cover every wall, the ceiling and even the floor, set in black frames that crowd edge to edge. Your reflection steps a moment after you do, and the room beyond the glass is always longer than the one you stand in. A pale doorway lies north, back to the hall, and an identical one waits south. You cannot tell which of the two reflected doors is the real one.
rooms.16208: Mirrors again, but cracked now, each pane showing a different slice of the room and none of them whole. A fine red dust lies in the cracks like dried wine. The door north leads out, though in the glass you see it standing on every side at once. South the chamber seems to go on, folding back upon itself until it ends where it began.
rooms.16210: This stretch of the hall is a second copy of the first, but wrong in small ways: the lamps hang on the left wall instead of the right, and the boards smell of cold ash. Doors stand east and west, one to a bedroom and one to a kitchen. The hall runs north toward a front door, and south an open archway shows a pale glimmer of glass. Somewhere a clock ticks, backward, you would swear.
rooms.16213: The front hall again, narrower than before, and its pegs are hung with long grey cloaks that keep their shape with nobody inside them. A door north opens on a covered threshold, a door east on the living room, and a door west on the library. The hall continues south. The floor tilts a few degrees to one side, and cold air creeps beneath every door.
rooms.16215: A narrow vestibule roofed in blackened boards, where the cabin's outer wall seems to have turned itself inside out. Lamp brackets jut from the planks at the height of your knee, and the floor is worn into a shallow trough by feet you cannot picture. The door south leads back into the front hall. Northward the vestibule opens on a road of pale, glinting bone.
rooms.16216: The path begins in earnest here, a road laid of skulls set jaw to jaw, thousands of them, polished by weather to the colour of old teeth. It comes up from the cabin porch to the south and turns to run east across a plain of broken grey ground. The sky above is the flat red of a wound closing. Every skull faces the same way, and it is not toward you.
rooms.16217: Thigh bones, long and yellow, are laid side by side in a herringbone, each end driven into the earth so that the path rings faintly hollow beneath your tread. On either hand the ground is cracked into grey plates with nothing growing in the seams. The way runs on east, and behind you it bends back west toward the cabin. A smell of old cellars rises through the gaps.
rooms.16218: Great curved ribcages have been planted along the road in pairs, arching over it like the ribs of some vast ruined hall. Between them the paving is a mosaic of vertebrae, each knob worn smooth by passing feet. A thin wind threads the arches and makes a whistling that is almost a tune. The path goes on east, and the arches lead back west.
rooms.16219: Bone dust lies ankle deep over the paving here, fine and white as flour, and rises in slow clouds at every step. Faint tracks of other travellers show in it, then fill and vanish. Ahead the road widens toward a crossing, and the dust blows across it in long pale ribbons. West the way goes back toward the arches, a dry rattle trailing after you.
rooms.16220: Four roads of bone meet here, though one of them has fallen away, and at the crossing a wheel of skulls has been set into the ground with the eyes all turned inward. Black cracks run out from the wheel like spokes. A path runs north, another south toward a gap in the paving, and the one you came by lies west. The hum you felt in your teeth is louder at this crossing.
rooms.16221: A single spine, a monstrous one, has been laid lengthwise down the middle of the road, its great knuckled links forming a raised ridge that you must step over. On either side lie scattered ribs, broken short. The ground beyond is a dead grey crust that crackles under the wind. The road runs north to another crossing and south to the one behind you.
rooms.16222: A crossing of bone pavements, rutted and sunken, where a thick black pillar leans out of the broken ground at an angle that should have toppled it long ago. The pillar hums, a low note that you feel in your belly rather than hear. Paths run north and south, and a third leads west under a drift of knucklebones. Dust lies in unmoving heaps on the pillar's windless side.
rooms.16229: The road turns a corner here between low heaps of jawbones, thousands of them, stacked with the teeth outward like rows of tiny fence posts. Grey grass pokes through them in wiry tufts. One path leads south toward a crossing and the other west along the bone road. The sky is a smear of rust and soot, and nothing at all crosses it.
rooms.16228: Tusks and curving horns have been set upright at the edges of the path, a crooked guard of ivory that bristles on either hand. The paving between them is flat shoulder blades, laid like scales, rocking a little underfoot. The road runs east toward a bend and west toward another stretch of the same. A smell of old copper hangs over everything.
rooms.16227: The paving is made of finger bones, millions of them, set on end in tight whorls so that the road looks tiled in pale grass. Walking on it raises a dry whispering like wheat in a breeze. Cracked black earth shows to either hand, dotted with thorn stumps that have never borne a leaf. The path runs east and west, and the same whisper follows you both ways.
rooms.16226: At this corner the road is paved with pelvic bones, wide and winged, fitted together like the plates of a great shell. In a hollow beside the verge a shallow pool of red water lies perfectly still, and no wind ripples it. One path leads east along the bone road and another south toward a lower stretch of broken ground. The air tastes faintly of iron.
rooms.16225: Small skulls, none bigger than a fist, have been mortared into low banks on both sides of the path, rank upon rank of hollow stares. The road itself is bare packed earth worn smooth, as if the bones were saved for the walls. North the path climbs back toward a bend, and east it descends toward a place where the view goes strange. A chill moves along the ground and does not rise.
rooms.16224: A baffling sight meets you here: the road ahead seems to climb and to fall at once, and the horizon shows twice, one above the other like a reflection hung in the air. A black pillar stands far off, upside down, its point resting on the ground. The bones in the paving lie in patterns that your eye reads as a face, then as a map, then as nothing at all. The path runs east and west.
rooms.16223: Knucklebones lie scattered over the road like dice thrown by a careless giant, and some of them roll a little when you are not looking. A crossing of bone pavements lies east, and the odd, shimmering sight is back west. Beside the path a low outcrop of black rock sweats a dark moisture into a runnel of dust. Overhead the sky is the colour of a bruise fading.
rooms.16230: The bone paving has been torn up here, leaving a long wound of bare red clay across the road. Bones lie in heaps at its edges as though thrown aside in haste. Rust-coloured water wells slowly into the deepest part of the gap. The road resumes at a crossing north of here, and a stretch of bone continues south beyond the clay.
rooms.16231: The road turns a corner here, paved with teeth set in black mortar, molars and fangs in rows, like an enormous mouth lying open to the sky. A shallow ditch runs along one side, filled with grey slag. The path leads north to a break in the paving and bends away east. A thin high humming runs through the ground and sets the teeth in your head buzzing.
rooms.16232: On each side stand shin bones driven upright in two close rows, a palisade of pale stakes as high as your waist. Between them the road is laid with long ribs lying flat, rattling underfoot. A low mist clings to the ground and hides your boots. The path leads east and west between the rows, narrow and straight.
rooms.16233: Every skull in the pavement here has an iron nail driven through its brow, rusted red, so that the ground looks freckled with old blood. Black thorn bushes crowd the margins, twisted into the shapes of reaching hands. East and west the road runs on, straight and hard. No sound rises from it but the tick of your own steps.
rooms.16234: At this bend antlers have been woven into a low barricade along the outer edge, their tines locked together like fingers. The paving is a rubble of hip and shoulder bones, loose and treacherous. A pool of dark stagnant water fills a hollow, and it mirrors a sky of a different colour than the one overhead. The path turns south, while west leads back along the road.
rooms.16235: Curling horns have been set into the road like rosettes, one at every pace, and small bones fill the gaps between them. A low ridge of black rock has risen here out of the broken ground and hides the view. The road comes in from the north and bends away east toward a break in the paving. Cold dew beads on the bone and runs into the cracks.
rooms.16236: The road has sunk into a shallow pit, its bones slumped and half buried in silt the colour of dried blood. Planks of bleached wood are laid across the worst of it, creaking and bowing when you step. East the bone paving resumes on firmer ground. West it runs back toward a corner, and a dry wind pushes dust down the length of the pit.
rooms.16237: Collarbones, thin and curved, lie in overlapping rows like roof slates, and they click like shingles under your tread. A black pillar stands a little way off the verge, taller than a house, humming so steadily that the dust trembles in time. The road turns here, leading north toward a straight stretch and west to a sunken place. Something in the air makes your skin crawl.
rooms.16238: A straight stretch of road runs between two long ditches filled with bone dust, and beyond them rise black pillars at even spaces, each as thick as an oak and humming on a different note. Together the notes make a slow chord that presses on your ears. The path leads north toward a gate and south back along the bone road. Nothing moves in the pale haze.
rooms.16239: The road ends in a circle of paving made of skulls, every one turned inward, while the way ahead is blocked by a wall of pale stone that rises crooked against the sky. A gate stands east, tall and leaning, and its shadow falls across the bones. The path you came by lies south. The humming is loud here, and the stone seems to answer it.
rooms.16240: A deformed gate rises before you, its arch pinched at one side and swollen at the other, the posts of unequal thickness and neither one quite upright. The doorway beneath it is too narrow at the top and too wide at the bottom, as though drawn by a child. Beyond it the walls of a vast pale building lean away with windows of every size. The bone road lies west, and the gate opens east.
rooms.16241: Just inside the gate, the passage opens into a cramped chamber where the walls lean together overhead and the floor slopes toward one corner. Corridors run along the outer wall north and south, and a wide archway on the east side opens onto a hall of pillars. The gate you came through lies west. Lamplight pools on the flags and then somehow fails to light the rest.
rooms.16250: A narrow passage runs along the outer wall of the building, whose plaster is scored with long scratches in groups of five. The ceiling is lower than it should be, and the lamps in their iron brackets throw crooked shadows. East the corridor continues toward a door set in the wall, and south it returns to the gate chamber. Your own steps come back from the wrong direction.
rooms.16249: A heavy door of black wood is set in the wall here, its handle at an awkward height and its hinges on the wrong side. The corridor runs east and west along the wall, and south a wide opening shows the columns of a great hall. North, a door leads to a place where the stairs wind. The floor is laid in flags of every size, none matching.
rooms.16253: A mindboggling staircase winds up from here, its steps turning in a spiral that seems to climb and drop at once, and each turn looks back on the last. Wooden rails are bolted to walls that bulge outward in places and sink in others. Far above, a square of grey light promises a way out, and the stair leads there. The door south opens back to the corridor of the wall.
rooms.16248: The outer corridor passes here beneath a row of narrow slit windows through which you can see only more wall. The plaster is damp and cold, and it smells of wet stone and old wax. East and west the passage continues along the wall, and a gap in the south side opens on the hall of pillars. A small draught moves, though no door is open.
rooms.16247: The corridor bends along the wall, where the floor is paved in black and white tiles that do not make a pattern but only a mess. Candles gutter in niches, burning with flames that stand perfectly straight. A large decorated door lies south, and the corridor runs back west the way it came. The tiles at your feet seem to shift when watched.
rooms.16246: A large decorated door stands in the wall here, carved with coiling shapes that begin as vines and end as writhing hands. It is set at an angle to the wall and yet seems flush with it. The corridor runs north and south alongside, and the hall of pillars opens west. The door itself leads east to a red and ruined shore, and a faint smell of blood comes through the planks.
rooms.16251: Black columns thick as ancient trees rise in rows from the floor into a ceiling lost in gloom, and each one hums its own low note. The floor between them is smooth and faintly warm, like the flank of a sleeping thing. Doors lie north and south among the columns, the hall goes on east, and west a leaning arch opens toward the gate chamber. Your voice dies a pace from your lips.
rooms.16252: More pillars, but these stand crooked and unequal, some no thicker than a man's arm and others broad as a cart, and a few lean on their neighbours like tired drunks. Their surfaces are marked with scratches that might be letters. Passages open north and south toward the wall corridors, a large decorated door lies east, and the forest of columns goes on west. The hum swells and fades like breathing.
rooms.16243: A door of black wood stands in the wall here, set so that it seems to lean out into the passage. Dust lies on the lintel in a perfect layer, as if nothing had touched it since the building was dreamed. The hall of pillars lies north, a corridor runs east and west along the wall, and south the door opens on a winding stair. A cold wind comes under it, though the air elsewhere is still.
rooms.16244: A single smoking lamp hangs here from a chain that rises into darkness without ever reaching a ceiling. Its light shows a corridor of cold plaster, with the hall of pillars opening to the north and the passage running on east and west. The floor is worn into two shallow grooves, as though a cart had passed again and again. A smell of tallow and damp stone clings to the air.
rooms.16245: The passage ends in a blunt corner of plaster stained with long dark runs, as if the wall itself had wept. North the corridor reaches a large decorated door, and west it runs back along the wall. The corner is not square, and when you stand in it your shoulder feels a gentle pressure. Somewhere a dripping counts out a slow, uneven time.
rooms.16242: Two walls meet in a corner that is not a right angle, and the floor has been laid to follow it in a long spreading wedge of flagstones. The gate chamber lies north. A door in the wall waits east. A shelf of grey stone is built into the plaster at about the height of your chest, with nothing on it but a ring of old soot.
rooms.16254: The winding staircase that began behind the door has been walled in, its steps vanishing under smooth plaster at the first turn. Chisel marks cross the plaster in anxious lines, as if someone had tried to dig back in. The air is close and smells of wet lime. The only way out is the door north into the wall passage.
rooms.16214: A second living room, larger than the first and twice as empty, with a sofa whose cushions have sunk into hollows that no one has filled. Picture frames cover one wall, each holding only a pale rectangle where a picture used to be. A clock on the mantel has no hands, and yet it ticks. The door west leads to the hall.
rooms.16212: Shelves rise in a spiral from the floor, curving around the room so that the volumes seem to lead you in while the door recedes. Every book is bound in grey cloth with no title, and when you open one the pages are blank. A single candle in a dish gives a light just strong enough to show how dim it is. The only door lies east, back to the hall.
rooms.16211: A narrow room with a narrow bed, its blanket folded in thirds and its pillow dented by a head that has not been there for years. A looking glass on the dresser has been turned to face the wall. A trunk stands at the foot of the bed with its lid shut and its lock bright as new. The door west leads back to the hall.
rooms.16209: A kitchen of stone, with a sink worn hollow and a pump whose spout drips a thin red thread that never fills the basin. Shelves hold jars of something pale and cloudy, each sealed with wax. A long table is scored with knife cuts, laid in patterns that look like maps. The door east returns you to the hall, and the smell of vinegar follows you out.
rooms.16204: A cold iron range fills one wall of this kitchen, its pots hanging above in rows from hooks, all swaying very slightly although the air is still. A pail of black water stands by the hearth and holds the reflection of a ceiling that is not above you. The tiles underfoot are greasy and uneven. The only way out is the door east, back into the hall.
rooms.16201: Shelves of dark wood climb to the ceiling and beyond it, so that the highest rows are lost in shadow, and a ladder leans against them with its feet on nothing. A reading desk stands in the middle of the floor with a lantern burning low upon it. The books smell of damp leather and old ink. The door east leads back to the hall, though from here it looks smaller than it should.

16255.description: The door in the wall opens on a ridge of dark gravel, and beyond it a lake of red water laps without a sound. The sky above is a low, bruised copper, and the air carries a warm smell like a butcher's yard. A shore runs north and south along the water's edge, while to the east the lake spreads away, thick and slow. The wall of the building towers behind you to the west.

16276.description: A narrow beach of black grit slopes down to the lake, and the red water slides over it in long, slow tongues that leave stains. Weed the colour of liver clings to the stones. The shore runs north toward a tall dark pillar and south back along the wall of the building. The lake itself lies out to the east, and nothing floats on it.

rooms.16283: A huge black pillar rises from the broken ground at the water's edge, as wide as a tower and taller than the eye can follow, and it hums so deeply that the pebbles at its foot shiver. The stone is slick, as if freshly wet, and shows no seam. The shore runs east along the lake and south toward a gentler beach. Overhead the clouds sit low and red.

16262.description: A strip of grey shingle runs between the building's blind wall and the lake, and the red water clicks against it in tiny waves. Dead reeds lean over the margin, their tips dipped in blood-coloured scum. The shore leads north toward the door and south to a dark pillar. To the east the water opens, still and wide, under a copper sky.

rooms.16269: A huge black pillar stands at the foot of the wall, and the shingle around its base is melted smooth into glass. The hum comes through the soles of your boots and sets your jaw aching. A path of scattered stones leads north along the shore and east along a rockier edge of the lake. Beyond, far across the water, the pale hump of an island floats in the haze.

16284.description: Jagged rocks, black and wet, jut out along the water's edge, and the red lake sucks at their feet with a small clinging sound. A huge dark pillar rises to the west, its hum running along the stones like a fever. The shore continues east, and south the lake lies open, its surface slow and thick. Crusted salt stains the rocks in rust-coloured rings.

16285.description: A broken terrace of grey boulders steps down to the lake here, each slab tilted at a different angle, so that walking it is a matter of leaping from one to the next. Rust-red lichen coats the stone in patches that look like old wounds. The shore leads east and west along the water, and south the lake spreads out, still and heavy. A cold, metallic smell rolls off the surface.

16286.description: The rocks are smaller here, scree and shingle slick with a red film, and they shift and clink under your boots. A dead tree, bleached and twisted, stands at the water's lip with its roots in the lake, and its branches dip into the red as though drinking. You can follow the shore east or west. South the lake is wide and quiet, with a faint steam on it.

16287.description: A wide shelf of flat rock reaches out into the lake, cracked into plates, and in the cracks stand pools of water so red they look like spilled paint. The air here is thick and sweet. East and west the shore runs on, and the lake lies south, motionless but for slow rings that spread from nowhere. The sky overhead has the dull gleam of old copper.

16288.description: The shore narrows to a ledge here, hemmed on one side by broken ground and on the other by the lake, which gnaws at the stone with a patient lapping. A mooring post, grey and split, leans from a crack with a loop of frayed rope still wound about it. A huge black pillar looms east where the ledge widens, and the shore runs back west. South the lake stretches away, dark red and still.

rooms.16289: A huge black pillar stands at the corner of the lake, rising out of a heap of fallen rocks, and its hum is so low that your heartbeat falls into step with it. The surface of the stone is polished and unmarked, and your face looks up from it, stretched. The shore runs south down the lake's far edge and west along the rocks. A crust of dried red stains the ground around its foot.

16282.description: The ground here is a bank of dark gravel pitted with little holes, as though the lake had breathed on it, and from the pits rises a thin red mist. A huge black pillar stands north, close enough for its hum to shake the grit loose. The shore runs south along the water, and to the west the lake opens, wide and dark. A sour smell like old pennies fills the air.

16261.description: Rocks like a broken stair lead down to the lake, and half-buried among them lie the great curved ribs of something that died here long ago, their tips sticking up like the masts of a wreck. The red water breaks against them in slow, oily folds. The shore runs north and south along the water, and the lake lies west, wide and utterly still. The wind carries a taste of rust.

16268.description: The shore here is a litter of black glass and shattered stone, as if lightning had once struck the ground repeatedly. Where the glass meets the lake it has melted into long smooth shelves, glossy under a film of red. The shore leads north to a bend and south to a dark pillar. To the west the lake lies open and silent, and the sky above it is copper and soot.

rooms.16275: A huge black pillar stands at the lake's lower corner, rooted in the stones, humming a note that rises and falls with the slow swell of the water. Its base is ringed with a cairn of small bones, heaped there by who knows what hand. A path runs north along the rocks and west along the bottom shore. The red water slaps against the pillar's foot and leaves no mark.

16274.description: Heavy slabs of rock lie tumbled along the water here, split and overgrown with a stiff red moss that crackles when touched. A huge black pillar stands where the shore climbs east, and the way runs on west across more rubble. North the lake extends, the surface smooth as a mirror and as dark. The sound of the water is soft and lazy, like breath in sleep.

16273.description: A strip of blackened gravel runs between the lake and a bank of broken ground, strewn with the splintered planks of some long-wrecked boat. The ribs of its hull stick up from the shingle, grey and rotten. You can follow the shore east or west, and north the lake lies still, the colour of a fresh cut. Tiny crystals of salt glitter on the stones.

16272.description: The shore is a low ridge of pale pebbles that clink like coins under your feet, and between them runs a thin stream of red water, braiding back to the lake. A bare thorn stands crooked at the margin with its branches all bent the same way. East and west the shore goes on, while north the lake spreads to the far haze. The air is damp and tastes of copper.

16271.description: Here the rocks climb a little, forming a small bluff above the lake from which the red water seems very far away and strangely flat. Pale lichen grows on the stone in the shapes of handprints, large and small. The shore runs east and west along the bluff's foot. North the lake extends to a pale smudge that might be an island.

16270.description: A rubble bank of black stone, tangled with dead roots like grey knotted rope, holds back a little bay of red water. The surface of the bay shivers continually, though no wind stirs. A huge dark pillar stands west, and the shore leads back east. North the lake opens and the haze closes in, hiding the other side.

rooms.16277: Your raft rides low on the Lake of Blood, and the water presses against its logs in a thick, unhurried swell. Close by to the west the grey shore slopes into the red, and a pale ridge of rock hides the wall beyond it. The surface carries a skin of scum that parts ahead of the raft and closes behind. North a rocky bank lies near, while south and east the lake runs on.
rooms.16278: The red water here is calm and heavy, and the raft turns slowly on it, as if it could not decide which way to drift. A film of oily bubbles gathers against the logs and pops without a sound. To the north the rocks of the bank loom close, and to the east and south the lake goes on, dark and unmoving. A low hum comes across the surface from the pillars on the far bank.
rooms.16279: A slow current tugs the raft toward the south, where a small island rises low from the lake, its pale stones just visible in the haze. The water is the colour of fresh blood near the surface and of old blood below. A rocky bank lies north, and the lake lies open east and west. A faint steam lifts from the swell and beads on your skin.
rooms.16280: The raft wallows in a hollow where the swell comes at it from two directions at once, and the red water slaps and chuckles around the logs. The air above is warm and sweet and sticks in your throat. North the bank of broken rock stands a short pole's length away. East and west the lake stretches out, and south it opens toward a wide red emptiness.
rooms.16281: Here the lake narrows toward the rocks, and the raft glides through water that is nearly black, with lazy threads of crimson turning on its surface. The pillar at the far corner of the lake sends a slow hum through the logs and into your boots. The bank lies close to the north and a stony beach to the east. West and south the lake falls away in long unbroken swells.
rooms.16256: Pale bubbles rise at intervals through the red water, and each breaks with a small flat sound like a sigh. The raft turns a half circle and settles again, its logs creaking. Not far west a dark shingle slopes up from the lake, and the wall above it is a blind grey cliff. The lake runs on north, south and east, quiet and enormous under the copper sky.
rooms.16257: The water here is shallow enough that you see, far below, the pale shapes of rocks standing on the lake bed like the stumps of a ruined town. Red mist drifts across the surface in slow rafts of its own. An island lies near, to the east, a low heap of stone in the haze. North, south and west the lake spreads away, and nothing moves on it.
rooms.16259: Close at hand to the west a low island rises from the red water, a rough knoll of grey stones with a few dead thorns on its crown. Ripples wander out from its edge in perfect rings, though nothing causes them. The lake lies open to the north and south, and eastward a bank of broken rock slopes into the swell. The air smells of rust and cold ash.
rooms.16260: A heavy swell lifts the raft and sets it down, and the red water beneath looks thick enough to walk on. The stony bank lies close at hand east, and above it the sky glows a dull copper. A trail of pale froth stretches away across the surface, behind the raft. North, south and west the lake goes on.
rooms.16263: Under the raft the lake is utterly silent, and the red surface reflects the sky with a stain of its own, so that the heavens look cut and bleeding. West a wide strip of grey shingle runs up to a wall of pale stone, and south a bank of black rocks curves in. The swell is slow and long. North and east the water stretches into haze.
rooms.16264: The raft drifts on a patch of water that is paler than the rest, a pinkish shade like weak wine, and in it floats a ring of tiny pale bubbles that circles without stopping. To the south the rocks of the bank rise near and sharp. North, east and west the lake spreads, wide and quiet. A faint hum shivers through the logs.
rooms.16265: An island lies just ahead to the north, a rough heap of stone and thorn, and the red water laps at its edge in long sticky strokes. Behind and around you the lake runs wide, and south the broken rocks of the bank slope down to the water. The swell here carries a smell of old copper and wet earth. A pale crust of salt rings the island like the line in an empty cup.
rooms.16266: The lake is darkest here, almost black, with veins of crimson running through it like blood in a bruise. The raft moves with a slow, unwilling sway. A stony beach rises close to the south, and the water spreads away to the north, east and west under a low copper sky. Far across the water, a tall pillar stands against the haze and hums.
rooms.16267: Close to the raft on the east side the bank climbs in black blocks, and a huge dark pillar towers over the far corner. The water here is warmer than elsewhere, and a thin red steam rises from it in curling ropes. South a stony bank lies near as well, and the lake runs on west and north. Every few moments the swell gives a deep, slow heave.
rooms.16258: The raft grinds ashore on a small island in the middle of the lake, a knoll of grey stone and dead thorn rising a few paces above the red water. The ground is cracked and pitted, and in its centre a ragged mouth opens between the rocks, with rough steps cut down into the dark. A warm, stale breath rises from it, smelling of ash and old bones, and the stair leads down toward a ruined city far below. The lake lies all around, and the swell runs away in every direction.
